sentences.text: This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the LAC no. 363/2016 (Award No.
08/200506/DC(NW)) Sumer Singh v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 15 requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid acquired land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.

5.
It is stated that the compensation awarded by the learned LAC is too low, unjust, arbitrary without any reasonable basis and the same is not acceptable to the petitioners.
The petitioners are recorded bhumidhars of the said land which has been acquired vide the said order.
The said land is very fertile and also gives handsome income to the petitioners in the form of 34 crops in a year.

6. It is stated that the said land is situated in village Rani Khera and is well connected with roads from all sides at the time of acquisition and LAC no. 363/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))

7. It is stated that the said land is situated near NH10 and is having a great potential value as a perfect building/commercial site.

The building activities and commercial activities is coming up for last more than 15 years and, therefore, the said land has great potential value and the market value of the said land is more than Rs. 10,000 per square yards.

It is stated that all kind of civic amenities i.e. electricity, water, road, bus service, telephone, school, college were situated in and around the said land and the said land has great potential value.

8. It is also stated that the said land is approachable by mettled roads and is very close to Mundka Industrial area which is fully developed at the time of issuance of the notification under Section 4 of the Act as adjoining areas situated in the vicinity of the said land have been developed as perfect industrial areas, therefore, the market value of the said land also requires to be assessed on the said basis which is perfect for industrial sites as well as it is close to Mundka Metro Rail Project.

There are many residential colonies in and around the said land, which shows the great potential value of said land at the time of passing of the notification under Section 4 of the Act and as such the said land could easily get Rs. 10,000 per square yards.

10,000 per square yards.

The assessment done by the learned LAC is totally wrong and illegal and the same should be rectified and compensation paid to the petitioners may be enhanced.
10.

Sumer Singh and has filed the present reference petition.
It is prayed that the petitioners may kindly be awarded the compensation of the land @ Rs. 10,000 per square yards along with statutory solatium and interest and other benefits.

11. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/LAC and, it is, inter alia submitted that the notification under section 4 was passed on 21.03.2003 and the declaration under section 6 of the Act was issued on 18.03.2004 and the land has been acquired for the public purposes i.e. for planned development of Delhi.
The notices under Section 9 and 10 were issued to the landowners/interested persons inviting claims/objections of the said land.

Pursuant to the notices,
claims were filed by the affected persons claiming different value of their land and, thereafter, the said award has been passed.

sentences.text: It is admitted that the claim of the petitioners with respect to measurements apportionment and compensation of the said land is admitted to the extent of the said award and the learned LAC has assessed the value of the said land in respect of the correct market value prevailing at the time of the notification.

Various factors were taken into account by the learned LAC while assessing the market value of the said land and, now the petitioners are claiming excessive and exorbitant enhancement of the said land and structures.
The Delhi Land Reforms Act is applicable to the said land and the petitioners are not entitled for compensation in respect of any construction or structure which is raised without sanctioning of law.
13. It is also submitted that the said land is not surrounded by any developed or undeveloped colonies and can only be used for agricultural purposes.
The petitioners have not filed any documentary evidence to support their claims.
The ld. LAC has categorised the said land into three categories on the basis of survey carried out as per the fertility and user of land.
The ld. LAC in order to assess the market value adopted the indicative price fixed by Government of NCT of Delhi for agricultural land in Delhi.

The learned LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land keeping in view all the aspects enumerated under Section 23 and 24 of the Act and has assessed the market value after considering the level of development, locality and situation of the area of the said land.

15. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award relating to village Rani Khera had taken into consideration the market value of the said land on the basis of the said sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available to ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

16. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by the ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

It is submitted that DDA is not liable to pay compensation for the said land which has been handed over to DDA and subsequently, taken back from the Land & Building Department from DDA and handed over to DSIDC.
17.

The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore, is not liable to pay LAC no. 363/2016 (Award No. 08/2005 06/DC(NW)) Sumer Singh v. Union of India Page no. 10 of 15 any interest on the delayed period.

The Award passed by ld. LAC is legal, adequate, just and fair and the same has been awarded by ld. LAC after taking into consideration all the factors relevant for determining the compensation, as such the petitioners are not entitled for grant of any enhanced compensation.

1. Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent ?
OPP 2. Relief.
20. Matter was, thereafter, listed for recording of petitioners evidence.

Counsel for the petitioners as well as ld. Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they both are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 238 of 2016 titled as Ram Kishan v. Union of India of Village Rani Khera.

I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  LAC no. 363/2016 (Award No.
08/200506/DC(NW)) Sumer Singh v. Union of India Page no. 12 of 15 WHETHER THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF YES, THEN TO WHAT EXTENT ?OPP 23.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.

It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by Unknown vs Union Of India on 16 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50305576/
6 LAC is always upon the petitioners.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
24.

sentences.text: To prove their case, the petitioners, through his counsel has adopted the evidence led in case Ram Kishan (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioner in the aforementioned case.
25. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.
LAC no. 363/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Sumer Singh v. Union of India Page no. 13 of 15 26.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera and covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

27. In the Ram Kishan (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 2005 06 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e.
an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Ram Kishan (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Ram Kishan (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
28 . The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.
LAC no. 363/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Sumer Singh v. Union of India Page no. 14 of 15 RELIEF 29.

It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by Unknown vs Union Of India on 16 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50305576/
6 LAC is always upon the petitioners.
Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera and covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
opennyai_summary.issue: 1. Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent ?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
24.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioner in the aforementioned case.
opennyai_summary.decision:
27. In the Ram Kishan (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 2005 06 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e.
an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Ram Kishan (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
28 . The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.
LAC no. 363/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Sumer Singh v. Union of India Page no. 14 of 15 RELIEF 29.
In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.
Unknown vs Union Of India on 16 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50305576/
7
(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii)Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv)Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
30.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
